close_reason: Updated README quick-start: TrustAnchor::try_from(Certificate), ValidationPolicy::new, validated.depth, '?' on CrlChecker::new.
description:
README.md lines 52-74 (the first runnable code block, the on-boarding example shown to every new user on crates.io and GitHub) has three independent compilation errors:

1. Line 64: `TrustAnchor::from_der(root_der)?` — no such function exists.
   Available constructors: TrustAnchor::new, TrustAnchor::from_cert(Certificate),
   TrustAnchor::from(&Certificate), TrustAnchor::try_from(Certificate).

2. Lines 66-69: `let policy = ValidationPolicy { current_time_unix: ..., ..Default::default() };` — `ValidationPolicy` is `#[non_exhaustive]` (pkix-path/src/lib.rs:554), so external crates cannot construct it with struct-literal syntax (even with `..Default::default()`). The struct's own doc at line 415 even says 'Construct via TrustAnchor::new ... Do not use struct literal syntax.' but the README does the forbidden thing for ValidationPolicy.
   Fix: use `ValidationPolicy::new(1_780_272_000)`.

3. Line 73: `println!("chain depth: {}", validated.chain.len());` — ValidatedPath has no `chain` field. Its public fields are `anchor_index: usize` and `depth: usize` (pkix-path/src/lib.rs:805-820).
   Fix: `println!("chain depth: {}", validated.depth);`

Bonus issue at line 81 in the next block: `CrlChecker::new(crl_der_bytes, now_unix, DefaultVerifier)` now returns `Result<Self>` (changed in P3 commit ff707564, PKIX-xjbw). The example doesn't `?` or unwrap it, so `crl_checker` would have type `Result<CrlChecker<DefaultVerifier>, Error>` and be passed by reference where `&impl RevocationChecker` is required — also won't compile. (Listed here rather than as a separate bead because it's the same README block; mark as resolved when the README is rewritten.)

Severity: P2 because this is the literal first example users see; broken examples damage onboarding more than missing docs would.

Pass-1 attribution: not addressed in commits 0d3e5db6..01908663 (P1 fixed pkix-chain doctest only). The README never tested as a doc build target; consider adding it with `cargo readme` or a custom test driver to prevent recurrence.
title: P2: top-level README quick-start example does not compile (3 errors)
